contracts.title: Provider and connection read DTOs never transmit stored secrets
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: consume server-redacted read DTOs, keep secret fields write-only, and retain defense-in-depth rendering redaction.
acceptance: Read responses omit secret values or return fixed redaction markers.
Secret fields are write-only in the published schema.

contracts.title: Physical devices and trusted-browser grants use distinct resource paths
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: use the distinct physical-device and trusted-browser-grant resources and their stable schemas.
acceptance: Physical-device and trusted-grant endpoints cannot collide.
Each endpoint publishes a stable response schema.

contracts.title: Device revocation reports every session and device failure
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: render the server's per-device and per-session multi-status result with stable retry keys.
acceptance: Optional stores are nil-guarded.
Bulk and single-device mutations return per-item status instead of unconditional success.

contracts.title: Device authorization preview identifies the requester and requested access
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: render authoritative client, scope, and expiry context and keep approval closed if a required field is absent.
acceptance: Pending-code preview contains client_id or client_name.
Pending-code preview contains authoritative scopes and expiry.

contracts.title: Email actions carry an authenticated action type
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: consume server-owned reset, verification, email-change, and invitation action flows.
acceptance: Reset, verification, email-change, and invitation links are distinguishable.
The action type is signed or server-owned and cannot be changed by the browser.

contracts.title: RFC 7592 reads are complete enough for lossless replacement
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: use the complete management representation for lossless GET-to-PUT replacement.
acceptance: GET and PUT return grant_types, response_types, contacts, tenant_id, and all persisted metadata.
A no-op GET-to-PUT round trip preserves registration state.

contracts.title: Dynamic registration schema, validation, and persistence agree
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: validate against the unified Discovery, OpenAPI, redirect URI, JWKS, certificate, and JWE contract.
acceptance: Published auth methods match validator behavior.
JWKS, certificate binding, JWE metadata, and redirect URI rules have one tested contract.

contracts.title: Registration access token rotation is recoverable
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: acknowledge the replacement token during the server's audited overlap window and never auto-retry an ambiguous update.
acceptance: A lost update response cannot permanently orphan management access.
Rotation provides idempotency, overlap, or an audited recovery flow.

contracts.title: JARM and redirect continuation are server-owned
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: follow only server-attested redirect targets and signed JARM delivery envelopes.
acceptance: The browser receives a validated redirect envelope or server-driven top-level continuation.
XHR/CORS behavior cannot consume or rewrite the authorization result.

contracts.title: Primary authentication, MFA, consent, and response delivery share one transaction
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: advance the one-time server transaction through primary authentication, MFA, consent, and response delivery.
acceptance: A one-time transaction records completed stages.
Network retry cannot replay credentials or consume an MFA factor twice.

contracts.title: Tenant usage uses a stable snake_case wire schema
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: consume the published snake_case usage DTO while retaining legacy-read compatibility.
acceptance: Usage DTOs have explicit JSON tags.
OpenAPI examples and contract tests match the emitted body.

contracts.title: Change requests expose a stable structured payload
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: consume the explicit structured JSON DTO and deeply redact rendered payloads.
acceptance: Change request DTO fields have explicit wire names.
Payload is structured JSON rather than an implicit byte-array encoding.

contracts.title: Runtime inventory and OpenAPI include every mounted console route
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: consume the published OpenAPI catalog and merge runtime feature metadata.
acceptance: Mounted routes are generated into OpenAPI and runtime inventory.
CI fails when route mounts, inventory, and OpenAPI drift.

contracts.title: First-run setup has explicit atomic or recoverable partial-success semantics
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: render committed resources and retry the server-issued idempotent application recovery envelope.
acceptance: The response identifies every created resource.
Partial completion supplies an idempotent recovery workflow or the operation is transactional.

contracts.title: Tenant branding cannot overwrite unrelated settings
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: edit a dedicated branding resource and require a current If-Match value for every mutation.
acceptance: Branding has a dedicated namespace or field-level patch contract.
Conditional writes prevent concurrent lost updates.

contracts.title: Snapshot detail never exposes credential material to ordinary admin reads
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: ordinary snapshot detail is unconditionally server-redacted; sealed artifacts remain a separate privileged concern.
acceptance: Server-side redaction is mandatory for readable snapshots.
Any sealed artifact download is no-store and protected by a distinct high privilege.

contracts.title: Restore and release operations expose durable progress and partial results
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: display the durable operation ID, steps, compensations, result, and failure after reconnect or restart.
acceptance: Mutations return a durable operation ID.
Step, compensation, and final states remain queryable after client disconnect.

contracts.title: Tenant lifecycle changes report credential-revocation results
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: report exact refresh-token and session revocation counts, failures, and stable idempotency keys.
acceptance: Session and refresh-token revocation failures are returned.
The caller receives multi-status or a retryable reconciliation job.

contracts.title: Break-glass grants and derived sessions have verifiable lifecycle coupling
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: create pending grants before credential minting, atomically activate them, and display every derived-credential revoke result.
acceptance: Grant creation cannot leave an untracked orphan session.
Revocation returns every derived-session result or compensates atomically.

contracts.title: Replay and cross-resource batch operations are idempotent and reconcilable
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: use atomic ReBAC batches and stable webhook replay claims so cleanup retry cannot redeliver.
acceptance: Webhook replay cannot redeliver solely because DLQ cleanup failed.
ReBAC and other batches return per-item status with stable idempotency keys.

contracts.title: Crypto administration reports exact retirement and rollout state
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: display source retirement status and the exact signing-key class and rollout state.
acceptance: Compromise actions report whether source keys were retired.
Rotation responses identify affected key classes and rollout state.

contracts.title: Federated OIDC and SAML callbacks resume the effective authorization request exactly once
contracts.frontend_mitigation: Resolved: Snaplink binds the complete federated request to provider state, hands the verified identity back through a one-use hosted-login transaction, and advertises authorization_request_passthrough_supported only when that continuation is configured. The console scrubs and consumes the transaction once, keeps older deployments fail closed, and accepts terminal delivery only from server-attested metadata.
acceptance: Federated GET binding preserves request_uri, request, repeated resource, authorization_details, claims, id_token_hint, and max_age before upstream redirect.
OIDC and SAML callbacks consume provider state before verification and resume account, policy, MFA, consent, and response-delivery gates without creating an unrelated session.
The hosted page removes login_transaction_id from the fragment before its one POST, skips concurrent provider discovery, and never replays an unknown outcome.
Terminal JSON responses attest the effective redirect_uri and response_mode and echo only the effective server-owned state.
